newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on foreign fund inflows.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on foreign fund inflows.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed higher against its U.S. counterpart on Friday amid foreign fund inflows and exporters' U.S. dollar sales, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.850 against Thursday's T$27.863 close. Turnover through dealers was a modest US$167.5 million.
Dealers noted some foreign fund inflows for the red-hot stock market, whose index closed 1.83 percent or 164.94 points higher at 9,192.57, a seven-year closing high.
"Some foreign equity funds flowed in, and exporters sold quite a few U.S. dollars," said one dealer.
Demand for the greenback was light because the New York market was closed for holiday on Friday.
The dealer also attributed the Taiwan dollar rise partly to the weakness of the U.S. dollar overseas.
For Saturday, a T$27.83-86 range was seen.
